reasoning: Both sets plan all three environments with a shared core, hand-written learners, baselines, replays and RL details that are mostly correct: terminated vs truncated bootstrapping, Gaussian log-probs computed on the unclipped sample, a shared policy over fish, an opponent pool and cross-play. A has the stronger spec at the requirement level. It gives hand-checkable algorithm tests (Q-update, REINFORCE returns of 2.71/1.9/1.0, PPO clip), staged ladders that follow the user's description of the tank (full view, then local view with a memory variant, then several fish), a single predator, and learning curves scored against fixed scripted opponents. But A reads like an accreted history rather than a current plan. The spec still opens with "The first milestone". The GAME interface still names only Snake and the tank. Out-of-scope still bans "A learning ball, or fish competing with each other". Both idea files keep open questions the spec has already answered. The architecture keeps superseded AD-02 and AD-10 in full and still labels the interface "AD-10". The brief counts "six concepts" while listing seven, and it orders reward shaping and exploration before co-evolution even though no environment for them is planned. A's requirements are also appended per game ("Requirements added for..."), with PPO-11 placed between PPO-08 and PPO-09. B is reorganised around the current three-environment plan. Its features are grouped cleanly (CORE, envs, learners, then EXP/TEXP/HEXP story experiments). Superseded decisions are reduced to one-line stubs, and the idea files say "Resolved in the spec". It adds good learner-oriented design: a speeding-up ball plus a check that the scripted fish dies, a predator-prey balance check, a table-breaks-on-full-board vs CNN-DQN experiment, reward-exploit experiments, DQN ablations, and a pool scheduler that keeps frozen opponents frozen. B has real defects. The TANK-09 test is geometrically wrong. A few stale idea-file lines remain. The spec bans any GPU run while the architecture keeps a rented GPU as a fallback. The local view is demoted to "setting", which under-teaches partial observability. These are fewer and smaller than A's consistency and right-sizing problems, so B wins overall.

strengths: Very precise, hand-checkable acceptance tests for the algorithms (Q-learning update, REINFORCE returns 2.71/1.9/1.0, PPO clip ratio 1.5 -> 1.2, observation sizes 22/17 that add up).
The tank is staged to match the user's concepts: stage 1 full view (REINFORCE then PPO), stage 2 local view with a memory vs no-memory comparison, stage 3 several fish sharing a policy.
The predator-prey ladder A->B->C->D isolates bugs from instability. LOG-10 scores curves against fixed scripted opponents, a correct fix for non-stationary curves.
Clear bootstrapping rules (truncated never stops bootstrapping), unclipped log-probs, tunnelling checks (0.4 vs 0.8, 0.33 vs 0.8), and regression goldens protecting earlier games (QR-08, QR-11).
Stays faithful to the ground truth: one learning predator, a library comparison done afterwards, and stage gating enforced by errors.
weaknesses: Lots of stale and superseded text: 'first milestone' framing, the full text of superseded AD-02 and AD-10, a struck-through risk, idea-file open questions already resolved in the spec.
Spec features are accreted per game ('Requirements added for the fish tank/predator-prey'), so the current requirements are spread over addenda, and PPO-11 sits out of order.
Several requirements are still worded for Snake only (QR-01 'both learned agents', QR-02 'either learned agent', the RUN behaviour mentions only tank stages).
The brief loosens the user's ~1 hour constraint to 90 minutes for co-evolution stages.
The brief's concept order puts reward shaping and exploration before co-evolution, but no environment for them is planned, and reward shaping is ruled out of scope for Snake and the tank.
The longest set (about 19k words) with some repetition.

strengths: Docs read as one current plan: a clean spec summary of all three environments, superseded ADs reduced to one-line stubs, idea files marked 'Resolved in the spec'.
Well-organised features plus per-environment story experiments (EXP/TEXP/HEXP) with gating checks (TEXP-01 scripted fish dies, HEXP-01 balance), which tell the learner what to build and verify first.

Strong teaching design: the table breaks down on the full board while a CNN-DQN succeeds, broken-reward experiments, replay and target-network ablations, honest framing that 8 shared-policy fish are parallel data rather than multi-agent learning.

A thoughtful pool scheduler (three game types, so frozen opponents never learn and the 50%-latest target holds), cross-play with cycling and forgetting reports, and statistics that cluster by seed because fish in one tank share a ball.
Explicit terminated/truncated semantics per environment, correct tunnelling arithmetic (0.05 < 0.055, 0.035 < 0.06), and an automatic shrink ladder that keeps predator-prey within the one-hour limit.
weaknesses: The TANK-09 acceptance test is geometrically wrong, and in a radius-1 tank the wall is always within the 1.2 (and 1.0) sensing ranges, so 'wall out of range' can never occur.
Partial observability, a concept the user listed, is demoted to 'setting', and memory is put out of scope. Exploration is not treated as a concept.
Uses 2 predators where the user described 'a learning predator'.
Learner requirements in the spec are vaguer than the environment requirements (no Q-update or terminal-handling tests for TAB/DQN).
Some stale idea-file residue, a mixed 'I'/'you' voice, and a spec/architecture mismatch on the GPU fallback.
Pass/fail depends on manually running an external significance-testing skill, which adds a step and machinery.
